scope: Token accounting/progress/excerpt sanitation; cumulative vs per-run usage; misleading inference counts.

findings.title: Excerpt redaction is bypassed by terminal-invisible code points deleted after redaction, reassembling the plaintext secret
findings.evidence: excerptText() calls redact(value) at line 97 and only then strips invisible code points at line 107 (isInvisible(code) ? "" : chars[index]). Inserting an invisible code point inside a configured secret defeats Redactor.text's replaceAll, and the subsequent strip deletes the splitter, rejoining the halves into the exact secret. Reproduced with 13 code points: U+200B U+200C U+200D U+FEFF U+00AD U+0001 U+0007 U+001F U+0085 U+0091 U+009B U+2028 U+202E U+2060. Reached from src/coordinator.ts:651 (trackExcerpt). The file comment at line 95 asserts the opposite ordering guarantee.
findings.reproduction: /tmp/rev30/probe/confirm.test.ts C1: excerptText(`model-${U+200B}secret`, Redactor(['model-secret'])) returns 'model-secret'. C2 end-to-end through the coordinator + publicWorker: an assistant message carrying the worker's own server_password split by U+200B is served by get_worker with the password intact (probe log: 'C2 leaks own server password: true'). The same works for the configured model API key and the freestyle API token. ANSI-split secrets do NOT leak (ESC becomes a space), which is why no existing test catches it.
findings.recommendation: Strip invisible code points before invoking the redactor (or move the redact call to after the character loop), then collapse whitespace and trim. Add a regression test asserting excerptText output for a secret split by U+200B and U+0007.

findings.title: inference gauge and excerpt entries are never cleared on reconcile-driven paused/recovery_required or poll-time guest loss
findings.evidence: Four transitions skip cleanup of this.inference and this.excerpts: reconcile paused (425), reconcile stopped->recovery_required (430), step() guest lost->failed (490), step() guest paused->paused (498). Guarded paths exist elsewhere (408-411 reconcile-lost, 849-850 control pause, 892-893 cancel, 966-967 destroy), so the invariant is clearly intended. runTick calls recover() before the per-worker step() loop (308-314), so a stopped/paused guest is normally reconciled into a terminal/paused state and never re-inspected, making the stale value permanent. Consequences: swarmforge_inference_requests_active (src/metrics.ts:80) and get_swarm_status.inference_requests_active (src/mcp.ts:287) over-report forever; get_worker keeps returning excerpt/excerpt_partial/excerpt_at for a failed worker, contradicting docs/MCP-API.md:8 and :35; both Maps grow without eviction.
findings.reproduction: /tmp/rev30/probe/confirm.test.ts C3 (step guest lost -> failed: gauge 1, metric line reads 1, excerpt served), C4 (reconcile -> paused: gauge 1 and excerpt present after 5 further tick+recover cycles), C5 (reconcile -> recovery_required: gauge 1 after 5 cycles). /tmp/rev30/probe/recoverfirst.test.ts R1/R2 reproduce the same via the reconcile-first ordering. Control: control(id,'pause') does clear both maps (gauge 0, excerpt null).
findings.recommendation: Clear this.inference and this.excerpts in all four transitions, or centrally when a worker leaves running/waiting without a result. Additionally gate publicWorker's excerpt on !terminal.has(state) && state !== 'paused' so the documented contract holds even if a cleanup path is missed.

findings.title: swarmforge_tokens_total labels every token row with the configured model, discarding the recorded per-message model
findings.evidence: render() calls store.tokens({worker_id}) which sums all five directions with no GROUP BY model (src/store.ts:328), then tokens.inc({team, model: this.c.config.SWARMFORGE_MODEL_NAME, direction}, usage[direction]) at lines 92-99. The usage.model column written at src/store.ts:30 and 307-321 is never read anywhere in the codebase. Rows recorded under a different model collapse onto the configured name, so the {team,model,direction} breakdown advertised in docs/OBSERVABILITY.md:16 is not produced.
findings.reproduction: /tmp/rev30/probe/confirm.test.ts C6: store.usage(worker_id,'m1','aux-model',11,0,0,0,0) renders swarmforge_tokens_total{team="other",model="qwen",direction="input"} 11 - the aux-model row is reported as qwen.
findings.recommendation: Select usage grouped by model (SELECT model, sum(input), ... GROUP BY model) and emit one tokens.inc per recorded model, using the configured name only as a fallback for empty model values.

findings.title: trackExcerpt and token-progress baseline key on the single current dispatch, so a cancelled-then-requeued turn can hide or misattribute the live excerpt
findings.evidence: trackExcerpt filters assistant messages to m.parent_id === d.message_id where d = this.store.dispatch(w.worker_id) returns only the first non-completed/non-cancelled dispatch (src/store.ts:236-239). If send_worker_message enqueues a follow-up and the earlier dispatch is then cancelled (store.cancelDispatches, e.g. from fail() or src/coordinator.ts:223), messages belonging to the still-streaming dispatch are ignored and the excerpt is deleted (line 643), reporting no progress while the guest is generating. The same single-dispatch keying drives the token-progress baseline at 612-618.
findings.reproduction: Code-evidenced only; not reproduced end to end within the budget. Related guard already covered by tests/excerpt.test.ts:204-212, which asserts a stale prior-turn message leaves the excerpt null.
findings.recommendation: Consider assistant messages parented to any unresolved dispatch for the worker, and stamp the excerpt with its originating message_id so text from a superseded run can never be presented as the current turn's live output.
